name: Kamāl al-Dīn Abū al-Barakāt ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Anbārī
summary: Baghdad grammarian of the Niẓāmiyya, author of al-Inṣāf, the book of the 121 questions disputed between Basra and Kufa, of the principles of grammar on the model of the principles of law, and of Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ, a ṭabaqāt of the grammarians.
bio: Abū al-Barakāt was born in 513/1119 and grew up in Baghdad, where he studied Shāfiʿī law at the Niẓāmiyya and grammar with Ibn al-Shajarī and al-Jawālīqī, and then taught grammar at the Niẓāmiyya. In later life he left teaching for devotion and lived in seclusion until his death in 577/1181. He is not to be confused with the Kufan Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī of the fourth/tenth century.

His al-Inṣāf fī masāʾil al-khilāf sets out 121 questions on which the Basrans and the Kufans disagreed, each with the arguments of both sides and his own judgement, usually for Basra: the book through which most later readers know the debate. In Lumaʿ al-adilla and al-Ighrāb fī jadal al-iʿrāb he gave grammar its own 'principles' (uṣūl al-naḥw) after the model of the principles of law: transmission, analogy and the presumption of continuity, with rules for argument. His Asrār al-ʿarabiyya gives the reasons of grammar for students, and his Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ, a history of the grammarians from Abū al-Aswad to his own time, opens with the story of ʿAlī's sheet.
